transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-17
Start: 09:30 PT
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Halcyon Eng Manager), Sofia Gomez (Halcyon ML), Tom Wu (Halcyon Infra), Priya Menon (Halcyon PM)
Artifacts mentioned: shared spreadsheet (link: drive.google.com/halcyon-pilot-batchflow), perf logs link (internal), security pack (Redwood drive)

--- Auto summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Quick throughput review from last week's burst test; avg steady-state tokens/s increased ~18% after batch tweak.
- Identified jitter during peak bursts; likely queueing and cold-kv cache warmup.
- Agreed next steps: run 3-node burst, share real prompt samples, Redwood to send Dedicated pricing + security docs.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, good morning, thanks for jumping on. quick roll call?
[00:07] Raj: hey this is raj here.
[00:09] Sofia: sofia present.
[00:11] Tom: tom, infra.
[00:13] Priya: priya, product.
[00:15] Liam: liam from redwood. maya on audio too.
[00:18] Maya: cool, thanks. agenda — quick perf recap, dig into the jitter at minute marks, then agree next tests and owners. sound good?
[00:26] Raj: yep, go ahead.

[02:10] Liam: ok so last Wednesday we pushed the continuous-batching tweak — lowered batch timeout from 20ms to 10ms for short sequences, bumped target concurrency per GPU from 6 to 8 for the pilot slice. net effect was average throughput up about 18% in steady state, but we saw more frequent micro-jitters on the 95th/99th pcts during burst windows.
[02:35] Sofia: can you define micro-jitters — are we talking token latency spikes or whole request stalls?
[02:40] Liam: mostly per-token latency spikes — you see the token RT jump for a few tokens while the kv cache warms or while a batch alignment happens. if requests line up oddly we hit a queue reshuffle.
[03:02] Tom: that matches what we saw in the infra logs — spikes correlate with brief CPU pressure on the RPC proxy, and occasionally a long tail when a request needs fallback to hosted lib (we had fallback enabled).
[03:18] Raj: hmm fallback — remind me which fallback we have active? hosted fallback or smaller-quantized model?
[03:23] Maya: currently we have both: model-variant fallback to a 4-bit quantized instance and a region fallback to our hosted pool if dedicated node busy. we can toggle either.
[03:35] Priya: is fallback causing state churn? for our use case some responses need deterministic traces, not approximate ones.
[03:41] Liam: good point — model fallback can change output slightly. we set it as safety for uptime but if fidelity matters we can prefer queueing with backpressure instead of fallback.

[06:05] Sofia: maybe run with model-variant fallback off for a controlled test? we want to measure throughput without semantic drift.
[06:12] Maya: yes we proposed that in the playbook. liam, can your team run a run-block where fallback is off and just let queue depth grow to configured max, then capture the SLO misses?
[06:21] Liam: yep we can. question — what concurrency target should we aim for? you previously said 8 per GPU, is that still target?
[06:28] Sofia: our latency SLO is 300ms p95 per request end-to-end. we'd like to push throughput while keeping p95 under 300. if 8 breaks p95 then lower.
[06:36] Tom: our infra budget prefers fewer nodes due to cost. we want recommendations for ideal concurrency vs cost tradeoff.

[08:55] Liam: quick note: continuous batching has two knobs that mattered — max batch size and batch wait ms (timeout). lowering wait reduces tail but can reduce batching efficiency. increasing max batch size helps throughput but can increase p95 when concurrency is misaligned.
[09:12] Raj: is KV cache preload possible for our cold-start prompts? we saw warmup spikes the first 30s of a ramp.
[09:18] Liam: yes, we have prefix caching and explicit prewarm APIs. in the pilot we didn't prewarm the full prompt set — if you provide top-5 prompts we can prime the KV cache to eliminate early spikes.
[09:30] Sofia: we'll share top-5 prompts and a 24-hour traffic slice. that should show realistic burst shapes.

[12:00] Priya: on the Dedicated vs Hosted question — we prefer Dedicated for PII workloads, but want cost comparator. can you send a price for a 3-node Dedicated pilot and hosted fallback hourly?
[12:10] Maya: yes i will include that. i'll add the security pack (SOC2 summary, encryption/KMS notes, audit log retention).
[12:18] Raj: any gotchas for VPC peering? our infra team is strict about IP ranges.
[12:22] Tom: yeah we have tight egress policies.
[12:24] Liam: we support VPC peering and customer-managed networking; we'll need your infra diags. tom can share CIDR ranges and peering constraints.

[15:40] Sofia: back to jitter — you mentioned queue reshuffle, can you walk through the sequence? like when we open N in-flight, how does the runtime decide to form or reshuffle batches?
[15:52] Liam: simplified: requests enter per-GPU queue, the batching thread tries to fill up to max batch size or until batch wait ms expires, then dispatch to kernel. if a long request remains it holds the slot, and a short request might be batched later. reshuffle happens when concurrent inflight requests exceed planned concurrency and we need to bump next batch alignment, causing some requests to wait for next cycle — visible as token latency spikes.
[16:22] Raj: so would increasing batch wait reduce reshuffle?
[16:26] Liam: yes up to a point — increasing wait improves batch fill but raises base latency; it's a tradeoff. for your short prompts we found wait=10ms hit best balance but with bursts you saw spikes.

[19:05] Tom: could backpressure at client-level help? e.g., throttle request spawn to keep queue below threshold?
[19:12] Liam: absolutely. we often recommend a client-side leaky bucket or concurrency limiter. Redwood also has route-level throttling and burst-capacity config. you can combine client limiter + server burst smoothing.
[19:25] Priya: do you have prescriptive numbers? like target concurrency per GPU for our model size?
[19:30] Liam: given your median seq len ~64 tokens and our optimized kernel, target concurrency 6-8 is reasonable; for steady-state aim 6, for aggressive throughput 8 but only if you accept some p95 risk. we'll validate in the 3-node burst test.

[22:40] Sofia: what about adaptive batching? can the runtime adjust wait or batch size automatically?
[22:46] Liam: we have adaptive heuristics (experimental in Dedicated) that modulate batch wait based on observed inter-arrival times. in hosted it's more conservative. we can enable an alpha version for the pilot if you want to test.
[22:58] Raj: are there any logs or charts we should look at to correlate spikes with CPU/RPC metrics?
[23:05] Liam: yes we'll share a waveform CSV and token trace with per-token latency, batch sizes, and proxy CPU.% — that'll let you correlate.

[26:10] Priya: security question — what about audit logs and retention for the pilot? we need minimally 90-day retention for compliance.
[26:18] Maya: Redwood supports configurable audit log retention on Dedicated; hosted has options via add-on. i'll put the retention options in the security pack.

[28:40] Tom: one more infra note — our egress/ingress NAT can add jitter; if possible we want peered private connectivity. what's the lead time for VPC peering?
[28:49] Liam: usually 3-5 business days to provision and verify peering depending on networking approvals. if urgent we can spin up a temp hosted tunnel to validate traffic shapes.

[31:15] Sofia: do we have benchmarks with similar median seq lengths on the model family we selected? we want apples-to-apples vs our predictions.
[31:23] Liam: yes we ran internal benchmarks on that quantization profile. i'll attach the perf spreadsheet. note internal benchmarks are synthetic; real prompt distributions matter, so please share your samples.

[33:50] Raj: recap — run three-node burst test with fallback off, capture logs, and test concurrency 6 vs 8; prewarm KV cache with top-5 prompts; share traffic sample; Redwood send pricing + security pack. correct?
[33:59] Maya: yes that's it. also liam will try alpha adaptive batching on a short run but won't enable it for the main test unless you sign off.
[34:10] Liam: yeah i'll do a quick alpha run and note differences.

[36:00] Priya: timeline — can we aim to have the test and logs by end of week? next Wed is a little late for us.
[36:06] Maya: we aimed for 2026-06-20 for the logs. does that work?
[36:12] Raj: yes end of week okay.

[38:30] Sofia: little nit — when you collect logs, please include per-request ids and route tags so we can map to our requests.
[38:36] Liam: will do; we'll include trace IDs and local request ids.

[41:05] Tom: also please include the RPC proxy metrics, CPU %, queue depth over time, and kernel occupancy.
[41:12] Liam: ack. we'll include all those series in the waveform dump.

[44:00] Maya: ok final checks — priya, raj, sofia anything else?
[44:07] Priya: nope that's good.
[44:09] Raj: all good.
[44:11] Sofia: good.

[44:30] Maya: thanks everyone. recap in email: liam runs 3-node burst test (fallback off) targeting conc 6 and 8, include waveform CSV, trace ids, kernel and proxy metrics; halcyon to share top-5 prompts and 24hr traffic; maya sends pricing + security pack. set next sync tentatively 2026-06-23 but we'll confirm after logs.
[45:00] Raj: thanks all.
[45:03] Tom: bye.
[45:05] Liam: bye.
